exemplars.title: PolicyPad: Collaborative Prototyping of LLM Policies
exemplars.why: PolicyPad gives collaboration, shared policy authoring, and private model experimentation persistent left–middle–right homes. The layout encodes a consequential shared/private asymmetry, allowing collaborators to coordinate around a common artifact while testing unfinished behavior privately.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over DynaVis because its fixed regions encode a more consequential social boundary—shared work versus private experimentation—rather than primarily organizing tools by technical function.

exemplars.title: DynaVis: Dynamically Synthesized UI Widgets for Visualization Editing
exemplars.why: DynaVis separates data, command entry, the working visualization, and synthesized editing widgets into four named functional regions. It is especially instructive because the stable panel framework gives dynamically generated controls a predictable home while their contents change.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over LLM-box vs. Thinking-box because all four regional functions are explicitly specified and together demonstrate how a fixed workspace can contain changing AI-generated interface elements.

exemplars.title: LLM-box vs. Thinking-box: Designing for Deliberate User Engagement with Distorted Information in Conversational Search
exemplars.why: The interface assigns stable regions to task framing, conversational search, and a repository for user-selected material requiring verification. Moving questionable content into a dedicated panel externalizes an epistemic workflow that would otherwise remain buried in the conversation transcript.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over EvAlignUX because its verification store has a sharper functional and interactional distinction from the conversation panel than EvAlignUX’s more conventional left-to-right evaluation stages.

notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order; scores were adjusted only slightly to reflect comparative structural fit. The evidence is unusually explicit about named regions and their functions, but it consists only of figure or system descriptions: it does not independently establish user outcomes, and persistence across an entire session is inferred rather than directly observed. Exact placement is also not stated in the quoted evidence for rid 5895.
